title: AI Sandboxes: A Threat Model, Taxonomy, and Measurement Framework
abstract: arXiv:2606.18532v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: AI sandboxes produce evidence about systems that may act through software tools, networked devices, or physical actuators. The interpretation of that evidence depends on the boundary of the experiment. We define a sandbox apparatus, distinguish five overlapping archetypes, and specify fifteen claim-relative measurement dimensions. A weakest-link licensing rule caps a deployment claim at its weakest necessary evidence dimension. We connect this rule to a threat model covering both outward harm and corruption of the evaluation apparatus, then apply it to four worked examples spanning driving, industrial control, tool-using agents, and vision-language-action manipulation. We also map the required artifacts to standards and regulatory instruments. The framework identifies which claims a bounded experiment supports, which failures its controls contain, and which assumptions require further validation before deployment.

translated_title: AI沙盒：威胁模型、分类法与测量框架
translated_abstract: AI沙盒为那些可能通过软件工具、联网设备或物理执行器进行行动的系统产生证据，而对这些证据的解读取决于实验的边界。我们定义了沙盒装置，区分了五种相互重叠的原型类型，并指定了十五个与声明相关的测量维度。一条“最薄弱环节”许可规则将部署声明限制在其最弱的必要证据维度上。我们将该规则与一个威胁模型联系起来，该模型同时涵盖对外造成的危害和评估装置本身被腐化的风险，然后将其应用于四个实例，涵盖自动驾驶、工业控制、工具使用型智能体以及视觉-语言-动作操控。我们还将所需产物映射到标准与监管文件中。该框架能够识别有界实验支持哪些声明、其控制措施能遏制哪些失效，以及在部署之前哪些假设需要进一步验证。
tldr: 该论文提出了AI沙盒的系统化框架，通过威胁模型、五类沙盒原型分类、十五个与声明相关的测量维度以及“最薄弱环节”许可规则，界定有界实验能支持的部署声明、其控制措施所覆盖的失效情形以及部署前仍需验证的假设。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a systematic AI sandbox framework—combining a threat model, a taxonomy of five sandbox archetypes, fifteen claim-relative measurement dimensions, and a weakest-link licensing rule—to determine which deployment claims a bounded experiment supports, which failures its controls contain, and which assumptions still need validation before deployment.
